text:
Ava (CFO): Thanks everyone who joined the ad-hoc finance office hours. Dropping a short public recap and a place to ask remaining questions. Main points: runway ~13.5 months under current plan, focusing headcount on revenue-impacting and infra resiliency roles, pausing discretionary capital until next quarter.

Sasha (Finance Ops): Procurement update: new quick thresholds to reduce approval latency — p-card <= $3k, PO w/manager $3k-50k, exec signoff > $50k. Were also centralizing small vendor contracts to reduce duplicate subscriptions.

Miguel (Sales): Curious about renewals budget for strategic accounts — can I still sign travel/ads to win deals?

Ava (CFO): Yes, strategic renewals & deal-closing activities are allowed. Require a 1-line ROI rationale in the Concur/travel approval or the vendor form and cc: your manager + Sasha. Tag as `#deal-critical`.

Tamsin (Recruiting): Hiring guidance? Do we still allow agency searches for senior ICs?

Sasha (Finance Ops): Agencies are limited to mission-critical exec/senior IC roles only and require a business case. Internal recruiters get priority for open reqs. Tamsin: well give you a roster of approved agencies this week.

Kian (Infra Eng): About the GPU buy vs cloud commit question: is prepaying for 1yr reserved infra allowed? How does that affect runway math?

Sasha (Finance Ops): We can prepay if it reduces unit cost materially and it's signed off by the Infra exec + Finance. For runway we treat prepaid commitments as committed spend amortized monthly. Example calc: `amort_month = prepaid_total / months_commitment`. We'll add a short worksheet for hardware vs cloud commit comparison.

Noah (Legal): Heads up on vendor negotiation: any contract with data residency, IP assignment, or indemnity clauses over $25k must loop Legal earlier. Use the vendor intake form and select the checkbox for "legal review".

Rae (Facilities): Office CAPEX question: can teams still request monitors/desk upgrades for new hires?

Ava (CFO): Day-to-day equipment for onboarding approved. Bulk CAPEX purchases (e.g., floor refresh) are paused. Fill the standard equipment request and tag `onboard-equipment` — finance will auto-approve up to $1k per hire.

procurement-bot: New vendor intake submitted by Miguel (Sales): https://forms.internal/vendor/541 - estimated value $42,000 - status: pending finance review.

Sasha (Finance Ops): Reviewing Miguel's intake now. Reminder: if you mark a vendor as `time-sensitive`, include a 1-paragraph risk note.

payroll-bot: Payroll notice: next headcount freeze review scheduled for 2026-02-01. Retroactive hires after this date may be flagged for review.

Miguel (Sales): Quick one: for partner co-marketing spend, is there a central budget or does each team fund?

Ava (CFO): Co-marketing is centralized. Send potential spends to Sasha + Marketing ops for prioritization; we will fund high-ROI partner activities first.

Kian (Infra Eng): If infra needs emergency burst capacity during an incident, who can greenlight a $30k cloud spend? Last time it took hours.

Sasha (Finance Ops): Emergency infra policy: on-call lead + Eng manager can approve up to $25k immediately. For $25-75k you need SRE exec + finance verbal approval; >$75k requires exec signoff. Finance must be notified within 12 hours for any emergency spend. We'll add the flowchart to the incident runbook.

Ava (CFO): Action items summary: Sasha to publish the updated procurement thresholds + vendor intake checklist by EOD Fri; Noah to publish a 2-line legal trigger guide; Tamsin to circulate approved agency list; Rae to confirm equipment auto-approve limits. Will follow up with a short FAQ doc and a pinned thread in #all-hands.

Sasha (Finance Ops): Office hours follow-up doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/finance/office-hours-1779043210 - drop any remaining questions here or DM me.

Ava (CFO): Thanks team. If anything urgent pops up over the weekend, flag with `urgent-finance` in the subject and tag Sasha.

End of thread.
